title: Stravinsky: The Rite of Spring
welcome_lead: 29 May 1913 — the riot at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: Stravinsky and The Rite of Spring 1913.
final_note: Rhythm seized the future of music.

concepts.def: Two or more keys sounding simultaneously.
Two or more rhythms sounding simultaneously.
Triad of two stacked major thirds.

walkthroughs.body_html: On 29 May 1913, the premiere of The Rite of Spring at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées caused a near-riot. Nijinsky's choreography and Stravinsky's dissonance, polymetre and ostinati shocked the audience.
Stravinsky stacks rhythms (3 against 2, irregular metres) and harmonies (the famous bitonal chord at the opening of Augurs of Spring combines E-flat major and F-flat major triads).
The Rite reshaped 20th-century music — rhythm and timbre took precedence over melody. Boulez, Bernstein and minimalists all acknowledged its debt.

mcqs.q: The Rite of Spring premiered on:
What is a tone row in serial music?
options: Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
A row of notes played together as a chord.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
A round where voices enter at different times.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
A recurring main theme (A) alternates with contrasting episodes (B, C, etc.).

sequence.def: 1894: Debussy's impressionism opens the modern era
1923: Schoenberg fixes all 12 notes in an ordered row
1952: ambient silence itself becomes the musical material
1956: Stockhausen fuses boy's voice and electronics
1964-65: Riley's In C and Reich's tape pieces start the style
